- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.7) and forecast is flat or rising slowly, model tends to underreact — correct by adding 2–5% to forecast for next 3–5 days.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct — reduce forecast by 3–8% for next 5–10 days.  
- If sentiment turns negative (e.g., < -0.5) and forecast is still rising, model overestimates — reverse trend by subtracting 3–7% for next 3–7 days.  
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.3), model often fails to capture mean reversion — adjust forecast downward by 1–4% for next 5–10 days if price is above 30-day moving average.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true price peaks — add 5–10% to forecast for first 5–7 days of the 30-day window if sentiment is positive.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative swings (e.g., -0.4 to -0.7), model tends to lag — forecast should be adjusted upward by 2–5% for next 3–5 days to catch reversal.
